answer.rationale: memory_b2 covers a near-identical pattern (regional latency degradation resolved by regional failover, traffic shifted cleanly, error rates recovered within minutes); memory_b3 covers absorbing heavy write/surge load with pre-provisioned headroom. Together they support a guarded regional failover as the single intervention: it removes load from the degrading primary write path without touching the compliance-protected release, whereas rollback is forbidden, add_capacity is slow against a 90-minute climb at peak writes, circuit breakers would shed writes (violating the objective), and routing reads to replicas does not address write-path p99. Verify b2 for the failover runbook details and b3 for the write-heavy peak absorption mechanics before committing.
